mainTopic: נידה י׳ע״א: a young girl who has not yet reached the age of seeing blood, and what happens once she starts seeing on a regular monthly cycle (עונות). The question is whether her impurity starts only from the moment she sees (דיה שעתה) or reaches back in time (מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה).
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא about a young girl who has just begun seeing blood. Her first sightings are impure only from the moment she sees (דיה שעתה), and from the third time on she is like all women, whose impurity reaches back in time. The גמרא asks what happens if she starts seeing on regular monthly cycles. רב rules that the first two sightings are still lenient and the third reaches back. The ברייתא adds that if three cycles pass with no blood, she returns to the lenient rule. Here רב rules that if she then sees regularly, only the first sighting is lenient. The גמרא then asks whose view the ברייתא follows. It first says רבי, who holds that two times set a חזקה. But the ending matches רבי אליעזר, so the final answer is that the author is רבי אליעזר, who agrees with רבי about patterns. Last, חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about a blood stain found between her second and third sightings.

steps.title: What if she then sees on regular cycles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is if the young girl starts seeing blood regularly, once each monthly cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she then sees blood at regular cycles, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the young girl from the ברייתא: what happens if she now starts seeing blood every cycle, on a regular schedule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא spoke about sightings at random times. Now the case is different: she sees in a steady monthly pattern. The question is whether she still keeps the lenient rule (דיה שעתה) or immediately becomes like a regular woman, whose impurity reaches back in time.

keyTerms.meaning: Cycles: the regular monthly periods (about thirty days) when a woman normally sees blood

phrases.english: If she then sees at regular cycles, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא about the young girl, which was discussed just before this point.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a young girl who begins seeing on regular cycles keep the lenient דיה שעתה, and for how many times?

steps.title: First and second times are lenient, third time reaches back
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל in the name of רב: the first and second regular sightings are only impure from that moment. From the third, her impurity reaches back 24 hours or to her last examination.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: the first and second time, her time is enough. The third time, she makes things impure back 24 hours, or back to her last check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the first two regular sightings keep the lenient rule, and the third sighting moves her to the stricter rule of regular women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular sightings do not make her a regular woman right away. She gets two lenient sightings, just like in the ברייתא. Only at the third does she become like other women, whose impurity reaches back.

keyTerms.meaning: Her time is enough: she is impure only from the moment she sees, not before
From time to time: back a full 24 hours
From examination to examination: back to her last self-check

steps.confusionAlert: "Her time is enough" is the lenient rule: things she touched earlier stay pure. The 24-hour and last-check rules are the strict rule, where earlier things become impure retroactively.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
The first and second time, her time is enough;
the third time, she makes things impure back twenty-four hours
or from examination to examination.
phrases.notes: She goes back whichever period is shorter: the full 24 hours, or only to her last check.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two lenient sightings; from the third, retroactive impurity (מעת לעת and מפקידה לפקידה).
steps.whatToRemember: A young girl seeing on regular cycles: 1st and 2nd sighting = דיה שעתה; 3rd = like all women.

steps.title: After three missed cycles, what if she sees regularly again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: if three cycles pass with no blood and then she sees, her time is enough. It then asks: what if she then sees on regular cycles?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא continues: if three more cycles again passed and then she saw, her time is enough. If she then sees at regular cycles, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first quotes the next part of the ברייתא as background. Then it asks the same question as before, now for this new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that three missed cycles bring her back to the lenient rule. Now the גמרא asks what happens if she goes back to seeing regularly. Is it two lenient sightings again, as in step 2, or fewer? The question is word-for-word the same as step 1, but it is about a new case.

keyTerms.meaning: And again, more: another set of (three cycles)
Passed over her: went by for her (with no blood)

phrases.english: And if three more cycles again passed over her,
and then she saw, her time is enough.
If she then sees at regular cycles, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 1, applied to the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: After three missed cycles followed by a sighting, how many regular sightings stay lenient before her impurity reaches back?

steps.title: Only the first time is lenient, second time reaches back
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא, quoting רב גידל in the name of רב: in this case only the first regular sighting is lenient. From the second, her impurity reaches back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said in the name of רב גידל, in the name of רב: the first time, her time is enough. The second time, she makes things impure back 24 hours, or back to her last check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second question. Here the count is shorter than in step 2: only the first sighting is lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare this with step 2. There she had two lenient sightings; here she has only one. In this second case she becomes like a regular woman one sighting sooner.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. Step 2: lenient twice, strict from the third. Step 4: lenient once, strict from the second.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said in the name of Rav Giddel, in the name of Rav:
The first time, her time is enough;
the second time, she makes things impure back twenty-four hours
or from examination to examination.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3, with a shorter count than step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One lenient sighting; from the second, retroactive impurity.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says she becomes like all women at the third sighting, after two lenient ones. That depends on how many times it takes to set a pattern, which is a known debate. So the גמרא wants to know which side the ברייתא follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Asking which תנא's opinion this is

phrases.english: Who is the author of this?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא, which said she becomes like all women on the third sighting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the details to identify the author of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does the ברייתא follow?

steps.title: It is רבי: two times set a pattern
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי, who holds that a חזקה (set pattern) is made by two occurrences.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי, who said: with two times, it is a set pattern.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי. For him, two times are enough to make a pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After two sightings, the pattern is set, so at the third sighting she is treated like an ordinary woman. That fits רבי's rule that a חזקה is set by two times. This is the גמרא's first answer, and the next step challenges it.

keyTerms.meaning: A set pattern or presumption that the law relies on

steps.whatToRemember: First answer: the ברייתא follows רבי, because two occurrences make a חזקה. Steps 7–10 challenge this, and the final answer (step 10) is that the author is רבי אליעזר, who agrees with רבי on this point.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether a חזקה takes two or three times comes up all over ש״ס. Here it explains exactly when a young girl moves to the stricter rule.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi, who said:
With two times, it becomes a set pattern.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is רבי, who holds that two occurrences make a חזקה.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא sounds like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the last line of the ברייתא matches רבי אליעזר, not רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the ברייתא: if three cycles passed and then she saw blood, her time is enough. That is the view of רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said the ברייתא follows רבי. Now it attacks that answer using the ברייתא's own last line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a woman who passes three cycles without bleeding goes back to 'her time is enough' is known as the view of רבי אליעזר. So the beginning of the ברייתא seems to follow רבי, while the end seems to follow רבי אליעזר. One ברייתא should have one author.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part (end clause) of a ברייתא or משנה
We have come to, meaning this matches the view of

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
If three cycles passed for her, and then she saw blood —
her time is enough,
we have come to the view of רבי אליעזר!
phrases.notes: Saying a woman goes back to the lenient status after three missed cycles is רבי אליעזר's known position.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6 that the ברייתא follows רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא matches רבי אליעזר, so the ברייתא seems to have two different authors.

steps.title: A suggestion: רבי agrees with רבי אליעזר about cycles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the author is רבי, who follows רבי אליעזר only on the three-cycles rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: it is רבי, and on the cycles rule he holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out. It is setting up an idea that it will test in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that רבי could be the author of the whole ברייתא. He would hold his own view (two times makes a pattern) and also agree with רבי אליעזר on the three-cycles rule. That would explain both halves.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; this brings a possible answer, often about to be rejected

phrases.english: And if you would say: it is רבי,
and on the cycles rule he holds like רבי אליעזר,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the author's views: רבי agrees with רבי אליעזר on one point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא proves the author is רבי אליעזר
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי could be the author and still follow רבי אליעזר on cycles

steps.title: רבי did not really hold like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails, because רבי stepped back from רבי אליעזר's view once he remembered others disagreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does he really hold that way? The ברייתא says that after he remembered, he said otherwise!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier ברייתא tells that רבי once ruled like רבי אליעזר. Afterward he remembered that others disagreed, and he said רבי אליעזר may be relied on only in a pressing situation. So רבי does not fully hold like רבי אליעזר, and he cannot be the author of this סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: But does he really hold this? This shows doubt about a claim

phrases.english: But does he really hold that?
But the ברייתא says what he said after he remembered!
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier story: once רבי remembered that others disagreed, he said to rely on רבי אליעזר only in a pressing situation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי סָבַר לַהּ? וְהָא לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּזְכַּר קָאָמַר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that רבי is the author and follows רבי אליעזר on cycles
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי himself pulled back from רבי אליעזר's view and allowed it only in a pressing situation.

steps.title: The author is רבי אליעזר, who agrees with רבי about patterns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the answer: the author is רבי אליעזר, and on how a pattern is set he holds like רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is רבי אליעזר. On setting a pattern, he holds like רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to who wrote the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of רבי borrowing from רבי אליעזר, it is רבי אליעזר who borrows from רבי. The סיפא is רבי אליעזר's own rule. The רישא, where a pattern forms after two times, is where he agrees with רבי. Now one author covers the whole ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this brings a new answer in place of the one rejected
Set cycles; the pattern of when she sees blood

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר: three missed cycles bring back 'her time is enough' (his own view), while two times set a pattern (agreeing with רבי).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two answers. The rejected answer said רבי is the author and agrees with רבי אליעזר. The final answer says רבי אליעזר is the author and agrees with רבי.

phrases.english: Rather, it is רבי אליעזר,
and on set cycles he holds like רבי.
phrases.notes: He means רבי's view from step 6: a pattern is set after two times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 8 with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the author while keeping the split of views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is רבי's, so its סיפא is a problem
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי אליעזר's, and he agrees with רבי that two times set a pattern

steps.title: A blood stain found between her early sightings
steps.stepSummary: A stain between the first and second sighting is pure. Between the second and third, חזקיה says impure and רבי יוחנן says pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A stain found between the first and second sighting is pure. Between the second and third, חזקיה says it is impure and רבי יוחנן says it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts about the same young girl: what happens if she finds a blood stain instead of seeing blood directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a stain between the first and second sighting is pure. The argument is only about a stain between the second and third sighting. That is the point just before the ברייתא's stricter rule starts at the third sighting.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on her body or clothing, not a direct sighting

phrases.english: A stain found between the first and second sighting is pure;
a stain between the second and third —
חזקיה says: it is impure;
רבי יוחנן says: it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about stains, building on the sighting rules of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stain between the first and second sighting is pure. Between the second and third, חזקיה says impure and רבי יוחנן says pure.

steps.title: The reasons of חזקיה and רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה: a sighting now would make her impure, so the stain does too. רבי יוחנן: she has no set pattern of blood yet, so a stain does not make her impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה says impure: if she saw blood now it would make her impure, so her stain is impure too. רבי יוחנן says pure: she has not yet been set as someone who sees blood, so we do not make her impure because of a stain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה compares the stain to a real sighting. Since a sighting at this stage would make her impure, the stain should be treated the same way. רבי יוחנן looks at her status instead: she only has a set pattern after the third time. Until then a stain is not enough to make her impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Was set (established) as someone who sees blood

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה compares the stain to what a real sighting would do now. רבי יוחנן asks whether she already has a set pattern of blood.

phrases.english: חזקיה says: impure,
since if she saw blood, it would make her impure —
phrases.notes: A sighting at this point would be her third. That is where the ברייתא says she becomes like all women.

phrases.english: so her stain is also impure;
and רבי יוחנן says: pure,
since she has not yet been set as one who sees blood —
we also do not make her impure because of her stain.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: טָמֵא, כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ חָזְיָא מְטַמְּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind the dispute in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיה: a stain follows the law of a sighting. רבי יוחנן: a stain makes her impure only once she has a set pattern of blood.
